notes: Faithful port of tab_descriptive_stats.R. Realizations repeat once per AI panel row (N=5,308), not once per quarter. ACF follows stored row order; e1071 type-3 moments are used. Series marked x1000 are divided by 1,000.
Supplied code: MAEs weighted by AI panel row counts through a duplicate join; randomization tests use signed mean errors, although the paper describes MAE tests. 10,000 draws, seed 20261031.
Shares count ties as AI wins, following the supplied R code; fractions are displayed (0.50 = 50%). Tests use 10,000 label swaps, seed 20261031.

Supplied code selects best AI persona across time, then compares the human MEDIAN on that persona’s quarters; it does not select the best human. Selection uses duplicate-join weights. Positional randomization is ported from R.

Ratios follow supplied code (unweighted quarterly MAEs). Stars use its signed-mean test and swap AI/Human within each ablation, not baseline/ablation labels. Recall cache combines older recall data with later BAA values.

Saved OOS errors use 2023Q1–2024Q4 and horizons 0/1/4; printed labels say 2024 and 0/1/2. Saved h4 errors are unclipped where current prepare_data.R would clip, so raw preprocessing is not fully reproduced. A 2024-only diagnostic is saved.

Historical reconstruction: older 492-row AI workbook, best AI per quarter versus HUMAN MEDIAN, evaluation targets through 2024Q4 (4/3/2 quarters). This differs from the caption’s best-human rule. The current-data/caption-method diagnostic is also saved; remaining mismatches are retained.
